summary_md: Zeileis, Koell and Graham (JSS 95(1), 2020; reprint run on sandwich 3.1-3) describe the sandwich package's object-oriented clustered and panel covariances: vcovCL (one-way and multi-way, HC0-HC3, G/(G-1) adjustment, odd/even inclusion-exclusion with an optional multi0 swap), vcovPL (panel Newey-West and Driscoll-Kraay), vcovPC (Beck-Katz PCSE) and vcovBS (clustered bootstrap). Worked examples reproduce multiwayvcov, plm and pcse to six decimals on the Petersen benchmark. On the Aghion et al. hurdle model, clustered SEs come out roughly 1.5 to 2 times the basic sandwich SEs. The Monte Carlo (10,000 replications, clusters of 5) finds CL-0 coverage near 0.95 across lm, GLMs, beta and count models once G is around 50 to 100. At G = 10, standard errors are underestimated, and the order from best to worst is HC3, HC2, HC1, HC0. The bootstrap is only somewhat better than HC0 and HC1 at that size. Panel NW and PCSE fail when panels are short or the dependence is exchangeable rather than decaying. The main relevance to Paul's systems is the Mentat sector growth study. Its two-way sector-by-year CR1 sensitivity in sgs_review.R is Equation 20 of this paper, implemented by hand. Its primary inference clusters by 5 to 9 sectors. That is below the paper's smallest tested G of 10, a size the paper already shows to be anti-conservative for CR1-type errors. The study's choice of a wild cluster restricted bootstrap with Webb weights, rather than CR1 t-tests, is therefore the right instinct. However, this paper does not test WCR bootstrap-t (its vcovBS is a variance bootstrap), so it neither validates nor refutes that choice. The SEATS-W test treats Newey-West HAC as secondary with no p-value, which matches the paper's finding that panel NW is unreliable. The paper has no bearing on networks, lobbying identity or allocation.

bearings.paper_claim: Eq 20 (Sec 3.2): the two-way meat is G_id/(G_id-1) M_id + G_time/(G_time-1) M_time - G_int/(G_int-1) M_int. Petersen benchmark (500 firms x 10 years) firm+year slope SE 0.053561 matches multiwayvcov. With one observation per id-time cell, multi0 substitutes HC0 for the intersection term.
bearings.paper_location: Sec 3.2 Eq 20 (text lines ~540-570); Sec 4.1 multi0 (p.13); Sec 5.2 (p.19-20)
bearings.system_side: The two-way sensitivity builds crv(sector) + crv(year) - crv(sector x year), each with its own G/(G-1) times (n-1)/(n-p). This is Eq 20 with an extra HC1-style small-sample factor. A non-positive diagonal is reported as not positive instead of being eigen-fixed (sandwich fix = TRUE).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The formula transfers exactly for OLS. A second path could check equality against sandwich::vcovCL(fit, cluster = ~ sector + year, type = 'HC1') on one study design. Until then the equivalence is UNVERIFIED (DE-062).

bearings.paper_claim: Experiment IV: at rho = 0.25 and G = 10, clustered SEs are underestimated in most cases, and about 50 to 100 clusters suffice for CL-0. The authors caution that the Petersen two-way result rests on only 10 year clusters, below what theory needs.
bearings.system_side: The two-way CR1 is computed whenever both dimensions have at least 3 clusters (SGS_TWOWAY_MIN_CLUSTERS = 3) and is tested with t on min(Gs, Gt) - 1 df. The study has 9 sectors over the 2020-2026 cycles, so every two-way cell sits below the paper's G = 10 floor. The code already labels the two-way result a fragile sensitivity.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper simulates balanced clusters of 5 with Gaussian-copula correlation and does not use two-way designs at G below 10. The direction (SEs too small) transfers, but the size of the bias for a 9 x 4 panel is not measured.

bearings.paper_claim: Experiment IV: for small G, the coverage order is HC3 > HC2 > HC1 > HC0, and HC3 is not found overly aggressive (contrary to Pustejovsky and Tipton 2018). The clustered bootstrap is only somewhat better than HC0 and HC1.
bearings.system_side: The CR1 error that enters the bootstrap-t is HC1-type, using sgs_cr1_factor = G/(G-1)(n-1)/(n-p). Primary inference is a WCR bootstrap-t with Webb six-point weights by sector. No CR2 or CR3 (HC2/HC3-type) cluster error is reported.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper does not test the WCR bootstrap-t (Roodman et al. 2019), so it cannot rank WCR against CR3. A CR3 or CR2 column for the focal term would be a cheap descriptive sensitivity. It changes no gate and needs Paul's go under change control.

bearings.paper_claim: Appendix A and Sec 7: panel Newey-West (vcovPL) and PCSE reach about 0.95 coverage only under decaying AR(1) correlation. Under exchangeable correlation or short panels, their coverage falls, while clustered HC0 stays satisfactory.
bearings.system_side: SEATS-W uses a residual moving-block bootstrap within cycle (3- and 5-week blocks, Holm) as inference. Newey-West HAC with Bartlett lags 2, 4 and 8 is secondary and carries no p-value.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's PL is a panel HAC over many short clusters, while SEATS-W is a weekly series within one cycle. Only the general point transfers: HAC alone is fragile when dependence does not decay.

gaps_exposed: No CR2 or CR3 small-G cluster-robust error is reported alongside CR1 in the sector growth study, although the paper finds HC3 best at G = 10 and the study has 5 to 9 sector clusters.
The two-way CR1 floor of 3 clusters per dimension is far below the paper's 50 to 100. Its df = min(G) - 1 t-test is untested at the study's 9 x 4 size.
There is no cross-check of the hand-rolled two-way CR1 against sandwich::vcovCL on the same design (a second path for DE-062).
flags: This entry is a methods and software paper. No conflict with D-021, D-025, D-104..D-108 or the rejected SNA proposals.
The 1.5 to 2 times SE inflation figure belongs to the Aghion et al. firm panel (803 company clusters). Quote it with that window and denominator, never as a general Mentat factor.
Bearings are agent analysis and stay UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces them (DE-062).
paul_alignment: There are no annotated-bibliography entries or annotations for this work (n_annots 0), so there is no takeaway to check or flag as stale. The built sector growth study already follows the paper's main lessons: cluster at the dependence level, distrust few clusters, and demote HAC.

related.why: This paper extends the 2006 sandwich bread/meat object-oriented framework (Zeileis 2006) to clustered and panel meats.
vcovPL and the HC0-HC3 corrections reuse the HC and HAC estimators from Zeileis 2004.
Imai and Kim cover point identification in two-way FE panels. This paper covers the variance of such estimates (sector and year FE, as in the growth study).
